content.title: CSS Investigation: Find the Rule
content.hook: Now we stop learning isolated properties and start investigating.
content.context:
A good CSS investigation asks three questions:

1. What should this element look like?
2. What does it look like now?
3. Which matching rule explains the difference?
goals: Apply the CSS concepts learned so far to locate the rule causing a visible problem and make the smallest correct change.

options.text: Two class rules match .note, and the later rule changes the color to white.
The browser cannot read class selectors.

feedback.correct: The matching later .note rule is the conflict. This is a cascade problem.
feedback.incorrect: The matching later .note rule is the conflict. This is a cascade problem.

activities.title: Repair the smallest thing
activities.instruction: Compose your response below, then submit to compare with the reference guide.

content.prompt: Fix the case without rewriting unrelated styles.
guidelines: One of them is causing the low-contrast text.
Remove the conflicting white color or replace it with a readable value.
content.sampleResponse: A clean fix is to remove the later .note { color: white; } rule. Another valid fix is to change that later declaration to a readable color when the requirement calls for it.

feedback.correct: A clean fix is to remove the later .note { color: white; } rule. Another valid fix is to change that later declaration to a readable color when the requirement calls for it.
feedback.incorrect: Please write a brief response (at least 10 characters) before submitting.

feedback.correct: The later matching rule changes the padding. Find the rule that is actually producing the current result.
feedback.incorrect: The later matching rule changes the padding. Find the rule that is actually producing the current result.

content.title: Investigation principle
content.text: Do not start by changing every property. Start with the property that best matches the symptom, then find the rule that controls it.

options.text: Change color, margin, padding, and font size until the page looks different.
Describe the symptom, identify the property that controls it, then inspect the matching rules for that property.
Add another matching rule before identifying the existing conflict.

feedback.correct: The second approach preserves information and narrows the search.
feedback.incorrect: The second approach preserves information and narrows the search.
